Why is ISRO’s NVS-03 satellite launch crucial? | Explained
 The mission could help restore the functioning of India’s regional satellite navigation system NavIC; its development began following the 1999 Kargil War, when the U.S reportedly clamped down on GPS data access
 Updated - October 30, 2026 11:14 am IST 
 Jacob P Koshy READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 GSLV-F18/NVS-03 Mission is scheduled for launch on 30th October 2026, at 23:51 hours IST from Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), in Sriharikota on October 30, 2026.
 | Photo Credit: ANI
 The story so far: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is scheduled to launch the NVS-03 satellite on October 30, in a mission that could help restore the functioning of India’s indigenous satellite navigation system, NavIC.
 The launch comes at a time when the constellation has been weakened by repeated failures of onboard atomic clocks and the inability to place its previous replacement satellite, NVS-02, in its intended orbit.
